chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn al-Tayyar who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If there do not remain in the earth except for two, one of the two would be the Divine Authority (Hujja).'

key_terms.الأرض: The earth — meaning all of human habitation; the statement is universal in scope
key_terms.الحجة: The Divine Authority or Proof — the Imam appointed by God as the living proof upon mankind, whose existence is a theological necessity

ai.seo_question: Does Islam require a divine authority (Hujja) on earth at all times?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms in this hadith the theological necessity of the Hujja — the divinely appointed proof and guide — being present on earth at all times, even if humanity were reduced to just two people. This teaching is central to the Shia doctrine of the imamate: that God never leaves the earth without a living authority who serves as the proof (hujja) upon mankind. The original audience, companions of the Imam in a period of intense theological debate with rival schools, would have understood this as a definitive statement on the indispensability of the Imam for the validity of divine guidance.
